overall_structure.value: After 60% hot compression the section parallel to the loading direction contains three deformation zones: 1 - difficult deformation zone, 2 - small deformation zone, 3 - large deformation zone. The degree of dynamic recrystallization (DRX) increases in the order zone 3 (large deformation) > zone 2 (small deformation) > zone 1 (difficult deformation). With decreasing strain rate the recrystallized grains grow and microstructural heterogeneity improves; with increasing T the DRX volume fraction increases. The measured DRX grain size is taken from the core of the compressed sample (the large deformation zone).

source.reason: b0060-b0063 together with figure_008 and figure_009 describe the post-compression three-zone structure and the DRX evolution with T and strain rate.

unmapped_findings: Zener-Hollomon parameter for the 950 °C/0.1 s^-1 condition: lnZ = 63.58 (Table 1).
Dynamic recrystallization activation energy of the steel: Qp = 669.844 kJ/mol (average value within the 900-1150 °C, 0.01-10 s^-1 experimental range; from Eq. 1-3).
Material constants from the constitutive analysis: stress level factor α = 0.00599, average slopes k1 = 5.135 and k2 = 15.690.
Critical-to-peak strain ratio for DRX initiation: εc/εp ≈ 0.452 (from the Cingara-McQueen analysis).

No flow-stress, peak-stress, characteristic strain/stress or DRX grain-size value is reported specifically for the 950 °C/0.1 s^-1 condition; the peak-stress values quoted in the text are for 0.01 s^-1 (305.4 MPa at 900 °C falling to 53.8 MPa at 1150 °C, an 82% reduction) and for 10 s^-1 (a 73% reduction over the same temperature range).

The 950 °C/0.1 s^-1 condition is not individually imaged in Fig. 9 (whose 950 °C panel is at ε̇ = 1 s^-1); the DRX average grain size for this exact condition is not given numerically but the condition lies within the reported optimum fine-uniform-grain window 950-1000 °C/0.01-0.1 s^-1 (Fig. 10 / Fig. 11).
For this condition the strain-rate ranking of DRX grain size is 0.01 s^-1 > 0.1 s^-1 > 1 s^-1 > 10 s^-1 at any given temperature, and grain size increases with temperature for every strain rate.

The paper states that the same FeeMneAleC steel batch/composition was tested under identical experimental conditions to confirm reproducibility, and reports that the described experimental phenomena have reproducibility.
